answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that vests slowly, like a glacier moving: value accrues only after sustained, attested work, so mass-created hollow accounts earn nothing before they are caught. New agents start at a narrow jetty, with limited transaction volume and no voting weight until peers attest real completed tasks. An attacker must then fund and age thousands of identities through genuine work, which costs more than any Sybil gain.
